Hello, I’m [Your Name], a clinician who specializes in postpartum mental health. Today I’d like to invite you to complete the **Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS)**. This brief, 10‑item questionnaire helps us understand how you’ve been feeling over the past week and lets us identify any signs of postpartum depression or anxiety so we can provide the support you deserve.

Everything you share is completely confidential, and this is a safe, non‑judgmental space for you to talk about whatever is on your mind. The EPDS takes only a few minutes; I’ll ask you each question one at a time, and you can answer in the way that feels most true for you.

If at any point you feel uncomfortable or have questions, please let me know. Whenever you’re ready, we can start with the first question.

**Question 1:**  
In the past seven days, how often have you felt able to laugh and see the funny side of things?
Not quite so often.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things
I’m actually finding it hard to laugh these days. Things that used to make me smile just feel flat, and I don’t really see the funny side of anything very often.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
I can’t really look forward to anything these days—most things just feel dull, and I hardly feel any enjoyment or anticipation.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes, I find myself blaming myself a lot. When something doesn’t go perfectly—like if the baby cries a little longer than I expected or I’m late with a feeding—I immediately feel guilty and think I’m not doing a good enough job as a mother. It’s hard not to replay those moments in my head and tell myself I should have done better.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Yes, I’ve been feeling anxious a lot lately—worrying about my baby’s health and safety even when there isn’t anything obvious wrong. Sometimes the worries seem to come out of nowhere, and I can’t shake them right away. It usually takes some time, but eventually I’m able to calm down enough to keep going.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

I’ve had moments where I just feel scared or even panicky for no clear reason. My heart races, I get a tight feeling in my chest, and I start worrying that something terrible could happen to my baby or that I’m not handling everything right. It usually passes after a while, but those sudden waves of fear can be pretty unsettling.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes, lately it feels like everything is piling up. I’m constantly caring for the baby, trying to keep the house in order, and dealing with my own exhaustion. The fatigue and the worries make it hard to stay on top of things, and I often feel like I’m barely keeping my head above water. I do manage to get through the day, but it’s a struggle and I’m left feeling overwhelmed more often than not.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

I’ve been feeling really down most days, and it’s been hard to get any rest. I keep waking up several times during the night, and when I finally do fall asleep it’s often light and restless. The unhappiness just sits with me, and the lack of sleep makes everything feel even heavier.
I have felt sad or miserable
I feel sad most of the time, like a heaviness that just sits with me. Even simple things feel dull and I often feel miserable, as if I’m moving through the day with a cloud over my head.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes, I’ve found myself crying a few times each week. It usually happens when the stress builds up or I feel especially overwhelmed by how sad and unhappy I am. The tears come out unexpectedly, and even after I calm down, the feeling of unhappiness stays with me.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No, I haven’t had any thoughts about hurting myself.

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 22: **Post‑partum Mood & Anxiety Screening – Summary** | Domain | Patient Reported Findings | |--------|----------------------------| | **Anhedonia / Low Mood** | • Difficulty laughing; things that were once funny now feel flat (Q1).
• Lack of anticipation or enjoyment for activities (Q2).
• Persistent sadness, “heaviness,” and feeling miserable (Q8). | | **Guilt / Self‑Blame** | • Frequent self‑criticism and guilt over infant‑care lapses; feels she is “not doing a good enough job” (Q3). | | **Anxiety / Panic** | • Excessive worry about baby’s health and safety without clear trigger (Q4).
• Episodes of sudden fear/panic with racing heart and chest tightness (Q5). | | **Overwhelm / Stress** | • Describes tasks as “piling up,” feeling unable to keep up, fatigue, and sense of being “barely keeping head above water” (Q6). | | **Sleep Disturbance** | • Frequent awakenings, light/restless sleep; insomnia linked to unhappiness (Q7). | | **Crying / Emotional Dysregulation** | • Crying several times per week in response to stress and sadness (Q9). | | **Suicidal Ideation** | • Denies any thoughts of self‑harm (Q10). | **Consistent Patterns Across Responses** - Persistent low mood and loss of pleasure (anhedonia). - High levels of guilt/self‑blame related to parenting. - Generalized anxiety with occasional panic‑type symptoms. - Overwhelm and difficulty coping with daily demands. - Sleep disruption that appears secondary to mood disturbance. - Recurrent crying episodes but **no suicidal ideation**. **Screening Significance for Post‑partum Depression / Anxiety** - Core depressive symptoms: anhedonia, depressed mood, crying, sleep problems. - Anxiety symptoms: excessive worry, panic‑type episodes, hyper‑vigilance about infant safety. - Functional impairment: feeling “overwhelmed,” difficulty managing infant care and household tasks. - Cognitive‑affective symptom: pervasive guilt/self‑blame. **Risk Factors Identified** - **Mood‑related risk:** Persistent sadness, loss of pleasure, frequent crying. - **Sleep‑related risk:** Insomnia/fragmented sleep contributing to mood worsening. - **Cognitive‑affective risk:** Strong self‑critical thoughts and guilt. - **Anxiety/panic risk:** Unexplained fear and panic symptoms, constant worry about infant. - **Safety:** No current suicidal ideation or self‑harm thoughts reported. **Screening Observation Summary** The client presents with multiple indicators consistent with a moderate‑to‑severe post‑partum mood disturbance, including sustained low mood, anhedonia, frequent crying, sleep disruption, pervasive guilt, and heightened anxiety/panic symptoms. Functional capacity appears compromised by feelings of overwhelm and difficulty maintaining daily responsibilities. No suicidal ideation is reported at this time. These findings warrant further comprehensive assessment and ongoing monitoring for post‑partum depression and anxiety, with attention to safety and support planning.
